title: Four consecutive integers with equal Euler totient

problemStatement.plain: Are there four consecutive integers that all share the same value of Euler's totient function? This is the k=3 slice of Erdos's strong conjecture; it is open even as an existence statement (no example is known).

proven: Run reduction: a length-(k+1) run of equal totients is exactly k consecutive members of A001274={m|phi(m)=phi(m+1)}; a four-run at n <=> n,n+1,n+2 are three consecutive members of A001274.
Record length-3 run at n=5186 (phi=2592), verified; does not extend to length 4 (phi(5189)=5188).
open: Existence of any four consecutive integers with equal totient (Erdos strong conjecture, k=3). No example known; none below 10^15.

currentState.focus: Formalized structural reduction + record run; existence remains open.
blockers: Existence is a genuinely open number-theory problem (needs three consecutive A001274 members).
currentState.nextAction: None tractable toward existence; structural layer complete.

papers: Kinlaw, Kobayashi, Pomerance, On the equation phi(n)=phi(n+1), Acta Arithmetica 196 (2020) 69-92.

insights: OQ-04 (four consecutive equal totients) is the k=3 slice of Erdos strong conjecture; OPEN even as existence — no example known. Not a witness-hunt.

KEY REDUCTION: n in CKE k <-> forall i<k, (n+i) in CET={m|phi m=phi(m+1)} (A001274). Four-run <=> three CONSECUTIVE members n,n+1,n+2 of A001274. Explains rarity: a single consecutive pair is already open/rare; four-run needs a consecutive triple.

Computational (this session): NO four-run below 10^8 (numpy totient sieve); only ONE three-run below 10^8, at 5186 (phi=2592). Literature (Kinlaw-Kobayashi-Pomerance 2020; Resta; McCranie, OEIS A001274): (5186,5187) is the ONLY consecutive pair in A001274 up to 10^15 => no four-run below 10^15.

Convention: galleried #1003 OQ siblings are pool-status completed even though the underlying existence/density questions stay open — the deliverable is the verified formalization + gallery entry, not resolving the conjecture.
